input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds the Customer (Bluefly) anywhere in the agreement. Section 14.8 (Personnel), the expected home for such a restriction, addresses only each party's supervision of its own personnel, IBM's right to assign its personnel, and IBM's subcontracting rights. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce" and "employ" return no restrictive-covenant language (only definitional and indemnity references to employees), and Section 14.16 states merely that "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others" — a freedom-of-action provision, not a covenant. None of the detection triggers ("shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce ... to leave") appear. This is our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline or counterparty comment is warranted. The duration and general-solicitation carve-out sub-checks are inapplicable because there is no non-solicit clause to measure; we should monitor any SOW or order documents for a re-introduced restriction and, if one appears, hold to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from end of involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, no no-hire).
